title: The Temporal Sequence of Party Leader Incongruence
description: High-density 64-channel EEG and linked behavioral data from 44 Dutch participants in a preregistered study of how partisans process political incongruence. Two tasks separate identity incongruence (Just Faces) from source-content incongruence (Statements & Faces), using supporters of GreenLeft/Labour as the in-party group and the far-right PVV as the out-party group. The dataset tests the 'Hot Cognition' hypothesis by examining the temporal sequence of neural responses to party leaders and their messages.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 64-channel BioSemi ActiveTwo system (10-20 layout, plus EOG, ECG and mastoid leads; CMS/DRL) and band-pass filtered offline at 0.5-40 Hz. Data were re-referenced to the average reference. Stimuli were presented with PsychoPy and data were analysed with MNE-Python. The Just Faces task had 260 trials, and the Statements & Faces task had 240 trials in a 2x2 design of face (in-party vs. out-party) by statement (pro- vs. counter-attitudinal).
